targets.title: A Life-Changing Event: First Births and Men's and Women's Attitudes to Mothering and Gender Divisions of Labor.
targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Baxter et al. (2015) is that becoming a parent leads [men] to more strongly support a traditional division of labor in relation to the care of children.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: The coefficient for “Male & had 1st birth” suggests that becoming a parent leads men to more strongly support a traditional division of labor in relation to the care of children (Coefficient = 0.13, SE = 0.05, p = 0.014). The reproduction sample included 14,553 individuals and 29,228 observations. The reproduction results are in line with the findings in the original paper (Coefficient = 0.11, p < 0.05, and a sample of 14,439 individuals and 28,857 observations). Consequently, this reproduction was successful according to the SCORE criteria.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: There were no deviations from the preregistration.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reconstructed original HILDA data analysis produces comparable numbers, but coefficient and sample counts differ beyond rounding. SCORE success reflects agreement in inference, not recovery of original numbers. One reconstructed focal model is reported, without sensitivity or alternative-specification checks; necessary reconstruction choices alone do not establish a robustness analysis.
